newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore industrial output down 7.6 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: Singapore industrial output down 7.6 pct in August.

text.p: Singapore's total manufacturing output fell 7.6 percent year-on-year in August due to a slowdown in the country's core electronics industry, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Monday.
The city-state's production of chemicals, transport equipment, plastic and petroleum products also declined, the EDB said in a statement.
Singapore's cumulative growth for manufacturing in the first eight months of 1996 was 6.4 percent, the EDB said.

Singapore's economy has been badly affected by the worlwide slump in demand for electronics due to its heavy dependence on this sector. Electronics and related products acount for almost half the country's industrial output and about 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
But the latest data shows the general economic slowdown appears to have spread further than the electronics industry.
The paint, pharmaceuicals and chemicals industry was one of the worst affected sectors, registering a 24.6 percent decline in output year-on-year.
